approved: Opposed the Infrastructure (Priority Funding) Amendment Bill 2013 as a crazy piece of legislation that would halt road funding nationwide until rail projects like Cross River Rail and Melbourne Metro, estimated by Infrastructure Australia at about $6 billion but likely more, are fully funded, and noted the Bruce Highway accounts for one in six National Highway fatalities.

Opposed the Infrastructure (Priority Funding) Amendment Bill 2013, saying the government has already delivered a 10-fold increase in rail spending, highlighted the $3.2 billion Regional Rail Link providing a dedicated line for Geelong and Ballarat trains into Southern Cross station, and warned an Abbott government would be the biggest threat to urban rail funding.

Opposed the Infrastructure (Priority Funding) Amendment Bill 2013, arguing it would defeat the purpose of Infrastructure Australia by mandating rail automatically take priority over road regardless of merit, and said the approach was driven by politics rather than an objective assessment of competing infrastructure needs.
